# tree-sitter-bash, vendored for sloplint

Date: 2026-10-20.

## Origin

- Upstream repository: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-bash
- Upstream tag: v0.25.1
- Published crate: tree-sitter-bash 0.25.1 (crates.io). Name and version are unchanged.
- This directory is the published crate plus the patch below. `README.md`, `LICENSE`,
  `queries/`, `bindings/rust/` and `Cargo.toml` are the published files.
- `sloplint-grammar.patch` is the diff of `grammar.js` and `src/scanner.c` against the
  upstream tag. It applies with `git apply` in a clone of tag v0.25.1.

## Why

The published grammar reports a parse error on valid Bash. sloplint skips a whole file on
any error node. These patches remove the errors that were reproduced on real scripts.

## Regenerating src/

- Tool: tree-sitter-cli 0.27.1, JavaScript runtime node v26.12.0 (the default).
- Command, run in this directory: `tree-sitter generate`
- It rewrites `src/parser.c`, `src/grammar.json`, `src/node-types.json` and
  `src/tree_sitter/*.h`. `src/scanner.c` is edited by hand and is not generated.
- The published `src/parser.c` was generated by tree-sitter 0.25.10. Regenerating with
  0.27.1 alone adds more subtypes to the `_expression` supertype in `node-types.json`.
  It adds or removes no node kind and no field.
- Run `tree-sitter test` in an upstream clone with the patch applied and the
  `test/corpus/sloplint_*.txt` files copied in. Upstream does not ship them.

## Changes to grammar.js

- Read-write redirect: `file_redirect` accepts the `<>` operator (`exec 0<> file`,
  `echo a<>b`).
- Here-string after a file redirect: `redirected_statement` takes one `file_redirect` or
  `heredoc_redirect` first. More redirects of any kind, here-strings included, may follow
  (`tee -a $c >/dev/null <<<"x $y"`).
- Lone assignment with a redirect: a new `redirected_statement` branch has the
  `variable_assignment` as body, with higher precedence than the generic branch
  (`Y+=" b" 2>/dev/null`, also `Y=a <<<x`). Without it the parser reduced the assignment
  into `command`, which then lacked a name. One conflict is declared for this:
  `[redirected_statement, list, command]`.
- Base-prefixed number with a variable: `number` accepts `simple_expansion` after `N#`
  (`$((16#$h))`, `16#$h`). `$((16#ff))` and `16#${h}` parsed before.
- Case pattern with several quoted chunks: `_extglob_blob` repeats the
  string/expansion/command-substitution chunk with an optional extglob part after each
  (`*"Copyright (c) "*"Uber"*)`).

## Changes to src/scanner.c

- Plain regex scan: outside `${...}`, a regex scan that meets an unnested newline now
  declines, as it already did at end of file. Before, a bare `==` argument (`echo == Loading
  $f`) made the scanner read on, across lines, to any later `)`, `]` or `}`, including one
  inside a string (rocksdb `generate_random_db.sh`). The check runs only when the plain
  `REGEX` symbol is valid and `CLOSING_BRACE` is not. The `[[ =~ ]]` right-hand side uses
  `REGEX_NO_SPACE` and does not reach it.

No other scanner change. An earlier version of this patch also changed how a backtick
starts a concatenated substitution. It is removed; see the first item under "still failing".

## Constructs verified fixed

Each was a parse error with the published crate and is valid for `bash -n`.

- `f() {` newline `tee -a $c >/dev/null <<<"x $y"` newline `}`
- `exec 0<> "${o}/fake-stdin"`, `exec 3<>file`, `echo a<>b`
- `case "$(echo x)" in *"Copyright (c) "*"Uber"*) ;; esac` (zap `checklicense.sh`)
- `Y="a" && Y+=" b" 2>/dev/null`
- `h=ff; x=$((16#$h))` and `echo 16#$h`
- `echo == Loading $f` followed by a line that holds `)` inside a string (rocksdb
  `generate_random_db.sh`). This is a scanner fix outside the spec table.

Shell files that now parse: 8 of 21 error files in the sweep (see below).

## Constructs known still failing

1. Two backtick substitutions in one file, the second opening across a newline (spec row
   "two backtick substitutions"; rocksdb `coverage_test.sh`, 2 files). Example:
   `G=\`a\`` newline `L=\`` newline `  b\``. The closing backtick of the first
   substitution and the opening backtick of the second have the same neighbouring
   characters, and the scanner sees the same valid-symbol set at both. Backticks inside
   the grammar are internal literals, so the scanner never sees the pairing. A fix needs
   the parity of the backticks, and the scanner does not track it.

   Tried and not kept:
   - Declining `_concat` when the backtick after the examined backtick is whitespace or a
     separator. It fixed both files. It changed valid trees: `echo a\` date\`` and
     `v=a\` b\`` split one word into two (bash keeps one word, `[aX]`), and
     `echo a\`` newline `b\`` changed shape. Reverted.
   - Gating on the `OPENING_PAREN` valid symbol: no effect on the two files.
   - Optional `_concat` before the closing backtick, combined with either of the above:
     the two files still failed.
   - A backtick external token with a depth counter: 18 of 27 calibration inputs changed,
     including `echo a\`\`b\``, `$\`b\``, strings, heredocs and `v=\`a\`w`. Abandoned.
2. `$((time -p "$@" >/dev/null) 2>&1)` (four golang.org/x/exp `shootout/timing.sh` files).
   Bash reads `$((` as arithmetic first and falls back to a command substitution. One
   attempt added a `$((` alternative. It regressed `echo $(( (a+b) * 2 ))` and was
   reverted.
3. Valid syntax that tree-sitter still rejects. Each passes `bash -n`. None is in the
   spec table, and none was analyzed further:
   - `"${{1#external/}}"` (bazel buildtools `buildifier/integration_test.sh` and
     `buildozer/buildozer_test.sh`).
   - `[ "$alpine" ~ "_" ]` (bun `scripts/bootstrap.sh`).
   - `for dep_soname do` (zeromq `android_build_helper.sh`).
   - bun `completions/bun.bash` and npm `lib/utils/completion.sh` (not analyzed).
4. `f() { :; } >f <<<x`: a function body with two redirects after it. Valid Bash. Still an
   error. A function with one redirect parses.
5. `exec 0> f` and `exec 0<> f`: the leading `0` is lexed as a command argument (`number`),
   not as a `file_descriptor`. The published grammar does the same for `0>`, so `0<>`
   now has the same shape. `exec 3<> f` gives a `file_descriptor`.
6. A lone assignment with a redirect followed by a command on the next line
   (`Y=a >f` newline `other`) parses as one `command` whose name is on the next line. The
   published grammar gives the same tree, because a newline is whitespace to the grammar.
   No parse error.

Invalid input that stays an error: `fbcode_config.sh` (`bash -n`: unexpected end of file).

## Corpus results

- Upstream `tree-sitter test` at tag v0.25.1: 100 of 100 before, 100 of 100 after.
- Vendored cases in `test/corpus/sloplint_*.txt`: 22 (redirects 9, case patterns 3,
  backtick concatenation 4, arithmetic 2, regex arguments 3, substitution 1).
  The published grammar fails 10 of the 22. The patched grammar passes all 22.
- Total with the patch: 122 of 122.
- The expected trees were produced by `tree-sitter test --update` and read by hand. No
  case contains an ERROR or MISSING node.

## Sweep result

Tree comparison between the published parser and this one on 1930 shell files (`.sh`,
`.bash`, `.bats` and Bash dot-files) from the cargo registry, the Go module cache and
`~/compiler`, including hidden directories. The files were frozen in a snapshot before
the comparison.

- Files with an error node: 21 before, 13 after.
- Files that changed from error to clean: 8. Files that changed from clean to error: 0.
- Files whose trees changed in any other way: 0. The other 1922 trees are identical.

Findings with `sloplint --no-cache` (release build): `meta/parse-error` goes from 6 to 4
in the registry and from 10 to 6 in the module cache. The sloplint walker skips hidden
directories, so the compiler sweep covers 26 files and shows no change. The only finding
removed is `meta/parse-error` on the files above. 932 findings were added, because rules
now run on files that used to be skipped. The largest are `grep/no-dynamic-symbol` (649),
`complexity/mutable-span` (161) and `grep/contiguous-log-literal` (76).

## Size

`src/parser.c`: 9,997,512 bytes (published: 9,912,254). States: 7597 (published: 7571).
